start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:keep-each-ais-identity-profile with store {\"where\": \"postgresql database example_me on my own computer\", \"language\": \"SQL (PostgreSQL)\", \"credential_name\": \"example-me-postgres-connection\"}, id \"ai-1\", name \"Ada\" and persona \"Patient and exact\"." It sets your AI's name and persona in your own database and reads the AI back.
no_lists_because: It names no list of its own: each AI's identity row is kept in the person's own store, in whatever form that store keeps things, and store says where and in which language.
instructions: 1. Keep the store's login in your vault under a name you choose, and say where the AI identity rows are kept and how the store is spoken to.
2. Say "Run workflow:keep-each-ais-identity-profile" with store, the AI's id, its name and its persona.
3. The first run makes the rows once and proves the writes and the reads on the example: every expected outcome and answer must match, or the run stops and says which.
4. Every later run sets the name and persona of that AI's row, keeps its other fields, and reads the row back with the defaults.

worked_examples.title: Name my AI Ada and give it a persona
worked_examples.ask: Call my AI Ada, with the persona Patient and exact.

store.where: postgresql database example_me on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The look step found no row for ai-1, so the write creates it; the prove step matched every expected outcome and reading.
worked_examples.hands_back: outcome "kept"; the row reads as name "Ada", persona "Patient and exact" and status "pending_setup".

worked_examples.title: A profile with no name is refused
worked_examples.ask: Save my AI's persona as Patient, but leave the name empty.

store.where: postgresql database example_me on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The name is empty, so the write has nothing to keep it under.
worked_examples.hands_back: outcome "refused", with the reason "a name is needed"; the row is not changed.
